connector: The book ends with the four kings and queens chasing the White Stag. They find a lamp-post, push through branches that turn into coats, and tumble out of the wardrobe, the same day and the same hour they left. Today you explain what the whole book is really about.

a.raw: the professor believed them and he didnt laugh
a.fixed: The Professor believed them, and he didn’t laugh.
a.why: The starts the sentence. The Professor is used as his name. A comma goes before and. Didn’t joins did and not.

b.raw: the four children ruled narnia and they made good laws
b.fixed: The four children ruled Narnia, and they made good laws.
b.why: The starts the sentence. Narnia is a name. A comma goes before and.

glossary.m: the big lesson a story teaches, said as a full sentence
a person who checks writing and fixes capitals, punctuation and spelling
the name of one particular person, place or thing, like Lucy or Cair Paravel. It starts with a capital.
a part of a word with one vowel sound. Garden has two: gar and den.
the main part of a word that holds its meaning, like port, which means carry
a comparison that uses like or as
telling the truth, even when it is hard

cards.title: World Notes: Mermaids in Old Stories
cards.sub: A real thing behind the story
cards.todo: Read the note. Then read with your lens in mind.
text: For thousands of years, sailors have told stories about mermaids, sea people who are half human and half fish. Stories say they sing beautiful songs.
Some scientists think sailors long ago saw real sea animals called manatees, swimming far off, and thought they were mermaids.
In Chapter 17, mermen and mermaids sing outside the eastern door of Cair Paravel for the new kings and queens.

transcripts.welcome: Hi, it's Opti. The four kings and queens tumble out of the wardrobe. Today you explain what the whole book is really about.
transcripts.guide1: Word work: build root words, fix a sentence like an editor, and spell by syllable types.
transcripts.guide2: Look back through the book. Then answer the questions.
transcripts.guide3: Today you give your response a title.

notes.wordParts: Roots from this year: inter = between, trans = across, form = shape, ject = throw, script and scribe = write, port = carry, struct = build.
notes.grammar: An editor checks in passes. Capitals for names and the first word. Apostrophes for belonging and joined words. A comma before and or but when it joins two complete thoughts.
notes.spelling: Syllable types: closed (cat), open (go), silent-e (bake), vowel team (rain), r-controlled (car), consonant-le (table).
notes.wgrd: The book ends where it began, at the wardrobe. The children are ordinary again, but the Professor says, Once a King in Narnia, always a King in Narnia.
vocab: the supreme ruler of a country or kingdom
the ceremony in which a ruler is officially crowned
restored to friendship or peace after a conflict

mods.script: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. After their fight, the two friends were blank. Sovereign? Hmm, no. Reconciled? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.

mods.todo: Read the before and after. Fix the sentence in the gray box.
mods.script: Be the editor. the witchs sledge was fast and edmund was cold. The gets a capital. Witch's gets an apostrophe. A comma goes before and. Edmund is a name. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence in the gray box.

virtue.name: honesty
virtue.title: Truth Watch: Is someone being honest?

items.t: In Chapter 2, Mr. Tumnus tells Lucy he was going to hand her to the Witch, and says he is sorry.
items.why: He tells her the hard truth, even though it makes him look bad.

items.t: In Chapter 4, the Witch tells Edmund she will make him a prince and then a king.
items.why: It is a trick. She only wants to trap him and his family.

items.t: In Chapter 8, Mr. Beaver says plainly that Aslan is not safe, but he is good.
items.why: He tells the truth, not just what sounds nice.
